study: Vignoles, Jerrim & Cowan (2015), Mathematics Mastery (Primary) — EEF cluster RCT (Ark developer/deliverer; UCL Institute of Education independent evaluators)
eval_evidence: 'Independently evaluated by Dr John Jerrim ... and Professor Richard Cowan (Institute of Education, University of London)', commissioned by EEF. Independent third-party evaluators with no developer stake; the program (delivered by the charity Ark) was the subject.
developer_evidence: The Mathematics Mastery program 'was delivered by the education charity Ark'; participating schools 'received training and resources to support the adoption of the programme' from Ark. The developer/deliverer charity delivered the PD.
cascade_evidence: Ark delivered launch training (1-2 days) and two in-school development visits plus multi-school workshops directly to headteachers, maths coordinators and class teachers; no train-the-trainer/lead-teacher cascade described -> developer_direct.
counterfactual_evidence: Waitlist design: control (Cohort B) schools continued business-as-usual maths teaching during the measured trial year before adopting the program the following year. During measurement the control got BAU with no alternative program -> business_as_usual.
coaching_evidence: School support = '1-2 days of launch training, two in-school development visits, three multi-school' workshops. Two in-school visits = a few light/periodic support visits, not recurring in-class coaching cycles -> occasional.
student_dose_evidence: Mathematics Mastery is a whole-class/whole-school maths curriculum approach taught by the class teacher; it changes only the teacher's regular maths instruction. No tutoring, pull-out, extra minutes, or student-facing software dose added.
maturity_evidence: Outcomes measured on Year-1 pupils after the FIRST year of program implementation in schools new to Mathematics Mastery (one year of implementation, immediate post-test) -> first_year.
